newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on stock/liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on stock/liquidity squeeze.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against its U.S. counterpart on Friday as tight money market liquidity forced investors eager to invest in the roaring stock market to swap greenbacks for local currency, dealers said.
The local unit closed higher at T$27.820 against Thursday's T$27.840 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$431.5 million.
Taiwan's overnight interbank rate closed higher for the ninth consecutive session on Thursday to reach a 21-month peak of 8.957 percent and rocketed into double digits on Friday.
The rate stood at 10.732 percent in late trade on Friday.
Dealers said the recently red hot stock market, which soared to yet another seven-year peak on Friday, has been sucking funds out of the banking system.
"The fund flow into the stock market took away money from the money market, creating supply shortage of the Taiwan dollar," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
But he said the local dollar's rise was curbed by persistent commercial demand for the greenback.
"Month-end and quarter-end demand for the U.S. dollar was still strong," he said.
A T$27.81-84 range was seen for Saturday.
